name: Restaurant host-stand ad boards
one_liner: Give restaurants a free sandwich board showing their specials, then sell ad space on it to other local businesses on annual contracts.
customer: Local small businesses that want to reach diners (e.g. realtors, gyms, dentists, home services)
offer: Year-long ad placements on boards placed at restaurant host stands, with the restaurant getting the board for free
how_it_makes_money: About $3,600 per year per ad slot. The case says one board can make $3,000 a month, and the business runs at about $10K a month with peaks of $15K after 6 months. There is also an upsell, but the transcript excerpt doesn't say what it is
startup_cost: low: stated as $0 plus printing; ads designed in Canva or ChatGPT
time_to_first_revenue: weeks: the case reached about $10K a month within 6 months
evidence: 'we are at about 10,000 a month... seen up to 15,000... doing this for six months' (McQucrnkSt0)
'sells ads on that board for $3600 a year' (McQucrnkSt0)
'How much money does it take to start? $0 and very minimal time' (McQucrnkSt0)
risks: Needs local, in-person selling to both restaurants and advertisers
Advertisers may not renew if they can't see results
UK ad prices will probably be lower than in the US
The more profitable upsell isn't disclosed in the excerpt

name: White-label GoHighLevel CRM for one local trade
one_liner: Rebrand HighLevel's all-in-one marketing, booking and CRM software as a product for one local trade and sell it as a monthly subscription.
customer: Local service businesses such as med spas, pest control, dentists, roofers, bounce house rental, dog walkers
offer: A CRM, booking, phone and AI tool under your own brand, set up with templates for that trade
how_it_makes_money: Monthly subscription. The example is $39/month. The public awards page shows gold-tier resellers have 100+ paying customers (at least $3,900/month), and some resellers make $50–150K/month profit by the presenter's back-of-napkin estimate
startup_cost: low-medium: a HighLevel agency or SaaS plan subscription (price not stated)
time_to_first_revenue: unknown: likely 1–2 months to the first paying clients
evidence: Public SaaSpreneur awards leaderboard: gold means 100+ paying subscription customers (VOo3M3ZHUoA)
'$39 a month... over 100 [customers]... at least $3,900 a month' (VOo3M3ZHUoA)
'pulling in 50, 100, 150,000 dollars a month of profit' (VOo3M3ZHUoA)
risks: Crowded market with many identical resellers
Customers churn, and support takes time
Depends on HighLevel's platform and pricing
Winning depends on picking an underserved niche; there's a possible opening in Portuguese-language or Portuguese-market trades

name: Premium AI-assisted B2B writing and editing
one_liner: Write high-quality, AI-assisted long-form content and sales enablement material for companies that are tired of generic ChatGPT text.
customer: Tech and B2B companies, marketing teams, sales enablement teams
offer: Blog posts and articles at $900–1,200 each, editing, and executive-writing training (one example was a 2-hour course)
how_it_makes_money: Per-article fees of $900–1,200 at about 5–6 hours each (roughly $90+/hour), plus training contracts
time_to_first_revenue: weeks: depends on having a portfolio
evidence: 'I'm charging anywhere from 900 to 1,200 per blog post' (tK5Ivv_3sEA)
Google Trends for 'hire a writer' dipped in 2023 and has risen over the past 2 years (tK5Ivv_3sEA)
The creator had an Apple editing contract and delivered an executive-writing course (tK5Ivv_3sEA)
risks: Income is tied to your own time
Requires real writing skill and credibility
Could be squeezed if AI keeps improving
Bilingual EN/PT is an advantage, but premium clients mostly buy English

name: AI personalised wall art and print-on-demand
one_liner: Sell personalised prints (posters, canvas, acrylic, metal) generated with AI on Etsy and Amazon, fulfilled by print-on-demand partners.
customer: Gift buyers on Etsy and Amazon (emotional, personalised gifts)
offer: Custom AI artwork, upscaled and printed on demand
how_it_makes_money: Per-unit margin on each sale. A comparable Etsy listing made 372 sales and $7,400 in 3 months, and an Amazon listing had 600 buyers in the past month
startup_cost: low: Etsy fees, Everbee, an upscaler, AI image tools
time_to_first_revenue: days to weeks (the claim of 'by the end of today' is hype)
evidence: '600 people bought this one in the past month' on Amazon (2wwkGPNmy_I)
risks: Very saturated market
Thin margins and ad costs
Etsy rules on AI-generated work and listing suspensions
Each personalised order needs manual work unless automated

name: AI product creative studio for e-commerce brands
one_liner: Produce ad campaigns, consistent AI model photo shoots and UGC-style videos for e-commerce brands using Claude/ChatGPT plus Higgsfield.
customer: Small DTC and e-commerce brands (phone cases, mugs, cosmetics, bottles)
offer: Monthly packs of static ads, 30-second video spots, and a consistent set of 3–5 AI models for site and social content
how_it_makes_money: Per-campaign fee or monthly retainer (no pricing stated)
startup_cost: low: Higgsfield credits plus an AI subscription
evidence: WEAK: 'when you're creating a brand for somebody, if you sell that service' (Mo3nUK9S8tI)
WEAK: demo of one prompt producing a finished 30-second spot plus statics and UGC (p3afXA65dIs)
risks: Prices are falling fast because brands can do this themselves
Tool-dependent, and AI models can look inconsistent
Ad platform rules on AI disclosure
No validated pricing

name: Email-your-network paid micro-consulting
one_liner: Send an AI-written email to a random sample of your network offering short paid consulting calls booked through a Stripe-linked calendar.
customer: Contacts in your network who value your expertise
how_it_makes_money: Per-session fee through TidyCal and Stripe (price and results not shown in the excerpt)
evidence: WEAK: 'create a 5-minute consulting calendar... with a Stripe integration. I'm going to sell my knowledge' (guJiTrw9qV4)
The six-figure goal is stated as a goal, not a result (guJiTrw9qV4)
risks: Needs calls, so it's not async
Limited by network size
UK GDPR/PECR rules on emailing contacts
No proven results shown

name: Returns and liquidation pallet reselling
one_liner: Bid on retailer return lots at a fraction of retail value and resell the items online.
offer: Returned or overstock goods (e.g. a $3,400 gazebo bought within a $200 lot)
how_it_makes_money: Resale margin. In one lot the Costco average item price was $628 and the bid was $62; the target was items worth a couple of hundred dollars each
evidence: 'Costco average price 628 bucks... average price on the bid is $62' (kEV86fy-Rvc)
A friend reportedly 'made millions'; the $10K-in-10-days challenge result isn't in the excerpt (kEV86fy-Rvc)
risks: Physical handling, storage and logistics
The US Costco supply chain doesn't carry over directly to the UK
Variable item condition
Ties up cash
